title: Fit the wave generator into a robot joint's mounted HSS-14 strain-wave gearbox
instruction: Fit the wave generator into the gear until it is fully home, then let go.
context: Robot-joint assembly technicians fit wave generators into mounted spline pairs when building strain-wave joints. This task isolates slowly rotating/rocking insertion on a StepperOnline HSS-14-50-I-D8 under about 10-30 N, figures obtained from the maker's technical support (Nov 2026). Motor fitting and powered testing follow.
setup: Millimetres; positions from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the bench. Robot-joint assembly bench. A StepperOnline HSS-14-50-I-D8 housed strain-wave gearbox (50:1, cup flexspline, cross-roller output bearing; maker's drawing: 73 flange, 34 from output face to input face, 38 h7 input register, 56 h7 output pilot, output 6 x M4 on a 23 circle, 11 H7 bore; simulated output face is plain and does not rotate) stands input side up, its flange bolted with 8 x M4 to the top of a one-piece black printed PLA cradle (120 x 120 x 10 base, 84 riser with a 56.5 bore, top 53 up), axis at x 290, y -90, input face 60 up (0.775 kg rigid housing/cradle body, estimate from maker's 0.51 kg whole unit minus 0.035 kg generator plus 0.30 kg cradle; an additional 0.050 kg mesh-stop proxy gives 0.825 kg articulated total in simulation). In its input bore the dark circular spline and the bright flexspline rim are mounted, rim level with the input face (bore about 31.0, obtained from the maker's technical support (Nov 2026); 1.0 lead-in estimate). The wave generator (drawing: separate detail views, 8 mm keyed bore; 14 hub borrowed from B detail; installed position 8.5 +/- 0.2, read as its hub end below the input face) has a 30.4 steel plug 8.0 tall with a 1.2 chamfer and a red index mark (estimates) above a 2 mm hub, and is clamped by its set screws on an 8 mm steel shaft (motor-shaft stand-in) carrying a printed black handle: 30 x 3 disc and 20 x 20 x 16 square grip knob, knob top 49.0 above the plug's bottom face (64 g in all, estimate). It stands on its hub on the 4 floor of an aluminium parts tray (140 x 100 x 15, 0.40 kg). Lot A: tray centre x 195, y -225. Lot B: tray at x 385, y -215, generator turned 90 degrees. At the back (fixed): the joint's NEMA 23 stepper (57 x 57 x 56, 8 mm shaft) on a printed 70 x 70 x 8 adapter plate at x 540, y 20, and the printed joint cover (80 x 20) at x 540, y -90. Real trial: gearbox $222.09 (maker's page, Nov 23 2026, pre-order), sourced partial kit subtotal $431.60, complete kit total unresolved; printable cradle and handle files supplied; dedicated replacement gripper pads; background motor disconnected. Proposed physical force logging uses a tared 5 kg load cell and HX711 interface at 80 SPS under the cradle; the scale and inspection tools are not rendered in simulation. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from overhead and side video (30 fps), a calibrated tared 5 kg load cell with timestamped 80 SPS conversions under the cradle, a caliper depth rod on the input face, a small square, and after the trial a dial indicator on the shaft. Heights are the knob top above the input face. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: the rolling 0.25 s mean of the load-cell readings exceeds 30 N (simulation: physics-step axial normal and friction forces across generator–stop and generator–housing/rim contacts at any offset/tilt, time-weighted 0.25 s mean; benchmark overload threshold); a gripper enters the input bore below the input face (rim marks under a 10x loupe, side video; simulation: within 17.7 mm of the axis, 0.5 mm or more below the face); the generator falls over about 8 mm (simulation: faster than 0.4 m/s) with no gripper on it anywhere but inside the gear; or the cradle moves over 5 mm, or tilts or turns over 5 degrees (tape marks). Score 0 at the end if the mesh is eccentric (dedoidal): turning the shaft slowly by the knob through two turns, it runs out over 0.3 mm on a dial indicator (proposed 0.5 N contact, unmeasured) 10 mm above the input face (derived estimate, checked against each specimen's own baseline at enrolment). In simulation the eccentric mesh is set by pushing the plug, on the gear axis, with measured touching-stop axial force of at least 20 N continuously for 0.25 s while it turns under 0.3 rad/s, or with measured touching-stop axial force of at least 8 N while tilted over 3 degrees, and cleared only by withdrawing the plug bottom to less than 0.5 mm below the input face. Otherwise, with the generator's axis within 1 mm of the gear's and tilt at most 30 degrees: 1.0 home (hub end 8.5 +/- 0.2 below the input face, the drawing's installed position: knob top 42.5 +/- 0.2; shaft square within 3 degrees), even mesh, both grippers at least 20 mm from the generator, shaft and handle, generator and cradle moving no more than 1 mm for 1 s (also below 20 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s); 0.75 home and even but held, or not still for a full 1 s; 0.5 the plug at least half way into the teeth zone (knob top 45.0 or less); 0.25 at least 1 mm into it (knob top 46.5 or less); 0 otherwise, including a generator lying on the rim or lifted out. Trials on lots A and B are averaged. The simulation also requires the mesh front to reach each credited depth and allows 0.5 mm plug-depth tolerance for the partial tiers (tolerated limits 45.5 and 47.0). The 30 N, 20 N and 8 N thresholds are benchmark estimates, not published bearing ratings.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B), averaged
reset_notes: Reset plan (untimed on a specimen). Ready-made HSS-14-50-I-D8 gearbox, bolted to the printed cradle once (fixture build: print about 5 h, tap 8 holes, bolt; not part of a reset). Drawing infers separability; the maker's technical support separately confirmed a separate part (Nov 2026): enrol only a unit whose generator is removable without dismantling its spline/bearing assembly. Enrol in 5-10 minutes (unmeasured): measure flange, register and pilot; fit the generator by hand, turning, to the installed depth; record two-turn shaft runout three times, each 0.10 mm or less, so the 0.3 mm cutoff is at least three times the specimen's baseline. Between trials, about 2-3 minutes (estimate, unmeasured): read the runout first, lift the generator out by its knob, reject fresh tooth marks, bearing roughness or looseness, check the output turns freely, and stand the generator on its hub at the next lot's tray centre, red mark toward +y (A) or -x (B). Keep the generator with its own gearbox. Check tape marks, zero the depth rod on the input face and tare and check the force logger. Fit dedicated replacement gripper pads; replace cut or greasy pads. Nothing is cast, cured, printed or powered per trial. Lead time 2-4 weeks; supplied greased, obtained from the maker's technical support (Nov 2026).
fidelity: HSS outline/depth; round cam collider; no flexible teeth. Drawing infers separation; maker support confirms separate part. Generator/stop impulses gate 10 N feed at 240 Hz, touch <=0.05 mm. Normal+friction count for the 30 N mean limit. Brake mu 0.4, equal reaction; HSS torque unmeasured. Feed 4 mm/turn, 20 N/8 N proxies and 0.3 mm runout unvalidated. Output rotation omitted; extra 50 g stop. 10-30 N insertion figures obtained from the maker's technical support (Nov 2026).
scores: Scripted demo: lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0 (mean 1.0). Dream-1: lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0, both at the 2,400-step limit. Two lots averaged.
